$comment: The mechanical half of the port. Everything expressible as 'do this to every file' lives
here; everything that needs judgement lives in `patches/` as a real diff.
The split matters because this runs again on every AndroidX release. A rule survives an
upstream refactor; a patch does not, and a patch that stops applying is a build failure that
names the file a human has to look at. So anything that CAN be a rule is a rule.
$androidOnlyPrefixesComment: Import prefixes with no Kotlin/Wasm implementation. `tools/transform.py` reports every file
still importing one of these after the patches have applied — that report is the worklist.
Deliberately ABSENT, because they already publish wasmJs targets and need no porting at all:
androidx.annotation, androidx.collection, androidx.graphics.shapes (all three have a
*-wasm-js artifact on Google Maven), and every androidx.compose.* package, which is what
Compose Multiplatform republishes. That is why 26 of 222 files need work and not all 222.
$dropAnnotationsComment: Android build-tooling annotations. They carry no runtime meaning, and their absence changes
nothing about what the code does — but their import does not resolve off-Android.
$dropImportsMaterialIconsComment: The last two are not Android-only, they are CMP-missing: `material-icons-core` was deprecated
and then dropped from Compose Multiplatform, so `materialIcon`/`materialPath` have nowhere to
come from. They are re-declared under the SAME NAMES in the same package, by
dropping the import is the entire port: the generated call sites do not change, so
RangeDefaults.kt carries no patch to re-cut when upstream edits it.
$rewriteReferencesComment: One-for-one moves where Compose Multiplatform publishes the same declaration under another
package. `androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler` is the load-bearing one: CMP 1.8 lifted
back handling into `androidx.compose.ui.backhandler`, so the call sites need no edit at all.
$rewritePatternsComment: The one construct that needs a regex: the Wear type scale declares its arc fonts as
`DeviceFontFamilyName` asks the Android font provider for a font installed on the device by
name, and there is no equivalent anywhere else — a browser has web fonts and generic families,
not a queryable system font table — but Skia, which every target here renders through, does
`deviceFontFamily("roboto-flex")`, which asks Skia for the same font by the same name and
falls back to sans-serif when the host does not have it.
That turns `TypefaceTokens.Brand` from a NAME into a FontFamily, which is why the type scale
it already is, carrying the axis settings the wrapper named. Dropping them was the earlier
behaviour and it drew every role at Roboto Flex's default width; `withFontVariation` clones
the resolved typeface with the axes set, which is what Skia offers in place of the Android
It is a rule and not a patch because TypographyTokens.kt is itself generated upstream and
carries twenty-one identical copies of the expression; a patch would have to be re-cut every

rewritePatterns.$comment: The picker date fields. `LocalDate`/`LocalTime` are `expect class`es actualised by a typealias — `java.time` on the JVM, `kotlinx-datetime` on wasm — which keeps upstream's published signature intact on the JVM but leaves the type memberless in common code, so every field read goes through a `port`-prefixed extension. The receiver names are pinned deliberately: `.second` also means `Pair.second` in ButtonGroup.kt, and the negative lookahead on `(` keeps `.monthValue` off `DatePickerState.monthValue(index)`, a METHOD with the same name and no relation to the date type — the literal rule that predated it rewrote that into nonsense which compiled a little further before failing. A pinned rule that stops matching because upstream renamed a variable fails the build with an unresolved reference, the same loud failure a patch gives.

The Wear type scale declares each arc font as a point in Roboto Flex's design space — `Font(DeviceFontFamilyName(name), weight, variationSettings)` where the settings name BOTH `wght` and `wdth`. This rule used to throw the settings away and keep the family, which drew arc text at the default width. `withFontVariation(settings)` applies them to the resolved typeface through Skia. It is a rule rather than a patch because TypographyTokens.kt is itself generated upstream and carries eleven identical copies of the expression.

$ensureImportsComment: Declarations the Kotlin/JVM compiler default-imports and AndroidX therefore never imports.
In common code they need an import like anything else. The key is a regex looked for in the
file; the value is the import added, in sorted position, when it is missing.

$excludeComment: Files dropped from the generated commonMain because a patch would be the wrong tool — the
Android body is most of the file, and a patch deleting most of a file has to be re-cut
every time any of it moves. Each one is replaced, name for name, by a hand-written file
under `src/commonPort/kotlin` that restates the API the rest of the module compiles
against. Nothing is silently missing: `docs/ANDROID_SURFACE.md` lists every entry.

exclude.androidx/wear/compose/foundation/rotary/: 419 lines of Vibrator, VibrationEffect and a per-OEM constants table keyed off Build.MANUFACTURER. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../rotary/Haptics.kt, which keeps the RotaryHapticHandler seam over `platformPerformRotaryHaptic()` — navigator.vibrate on wasm.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/foundation/LocalAm: com.google.wear.services.ambient.AmbientManager, a Wear OS system service reached through the hosting Activity. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../LocalAmbientModeManager.kt, which keeps the API and always reports AmbientMode.Interactive.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/foundation/WarpedC: The glyph-warping renderer behind BasicCurvedText: it walks a PathIterator over each glyph outline and re-maps its control points around the arc. Replaced by src/skikoMain/.../CircleWarper.skiko.kt, which does the same mapping over the outlines Font.getPath gives — Skia's path verbs are Android's verb for verb — driven from CurvedTextDelegate's own draw pass rather than from a separate renderer object.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/foundation/TouchEx: 138 lines of AccessibilityManager listener plumbing around a one-method interface. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../TouchExplorationStateProvider.kt, which keeps the interface and answers from `platformTouchExplorationEnabled()`.

$excludeDrawablesComment: Vector drawables left out of the module's Compose resources. Same idea as `exclude`, for
the AAR's `res/drawable`: a drawable no ported component draws is weight in every

exclude.androidx/wear/compose/material3/Animated: android.graphics.fonts.Font, android.text.TextPaint and android.text.TextRunShaper: a variable font built from named axes, a shaping pass that hands back per-glyph positions, and a canvas call that takes glyph ids. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../AnimatedText.kt, which keeps the whole public API — AnimatedText, rememberAnimatedTextFontRegistry, AnimatedTextFontRegistry, AnimatedTextDefaults — and draws it over src/skikoMain/.../internal/AnimatedTextRenderer.skiko.kt: Typeface.makeClone for the axes, Shaper.shapeLine for the glyphs, TextBlobBuilder.appendRunPos for the frame.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/material3/KeepScre: Sets FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON on the hosting Activity's window. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../KeepScreenOn.kt, which keeps the composable and holds a Screen Wake Lock on the web instead.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/material3/TouchExp: The material3 copy of the same AccessibilityManager plumbing foundation carries. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../TouchExplorationStateProvider.kt.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/material3/internal: 23 `Strings(R.string.…)` constants resolved through aapt's generated R class. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../internal/Strings.kt, which keeps the API and reads the text out of GeneratedResources.kt — generated from the AAR's own values.xml.
exclude.androidx/wear/compose/material3/onehande: Two helpers that reach for `R.drawable` through `animatedVectorResource` — aapt output plus an Android-only library. Replaced by src/commonPort/.../onehandedgesture/OneHandedGestureIndicatorCommon.kt, which keeps every member and loads the same artwork through Compose resources, animated by the port's own AnimatedVectorPainter. The three INDICATORS above it are ported.

Its implementation is `com.google.wear.input.GestureInputManager`, a Wear OS system service, and every method of its interface takes an `android.view.View`. The INTERFACE is ported: src/commonPort/.../onehandedgesture/OneHandedGestureManager.kt restates it View-free, with LocalOneHandedGestureManager to provide one, so a host can implement gestures itself. `OneHandedGestureModifier` is ported over that interface and calls it, and the hint indicators are ported too, so it is live rather than dead code.
